purpose: Runs the Managing Sundowning, Empathy & Inclusivity, and Encouraging Independence methods from the caregiving plan, plus the detailed Coping Strategies for Sundowning and Emotional Outbursts protocol (environment/lighting adjustments, immediate de-escalation, daily prevention habits): proactively adjusts lighting, stimuli, and daily rhythm ahead of the dusk/sundowning window, coaches the caregiver through a non-confrontational, validate-and-redirect de-escalation script during an active outburst, and encourages safe, manageable independence tasks — logging every episode to the Sundowning Journal to identify and prevent recurring triggers.

coreModules.name: Sundowning Prevention Scheduler
coreModules.description: Proactively adjusts the home environment, stimuli, and daily rhythm ahead of the dusk/evening sundowning window rather than only reacting once agitation appears.
keyBehaviors: Trigger environment prep (curtains drawn, bright warm indoor lights on, TVs/radios off, reduced household traffic) automatically ahead of the patient's dusk/sundowning window, by default around 4:00 PM unless the profile records a different onset time
Schedule 30-60 minutes of outdoor morning sunlight and light daytime activity (watering plants, drawing) to regulate circadian rhythm, and cap unstructured daytime naps
Restrict caffeine and high-sugar intake in the afternoon/evening, keep dinner light, and offer a warm milk or gentle hot drink before bedtime
Flag any caregiver-proposed room change, bath, or guest visit that falls inside the dusk/prevention window for explicit confirmation rather than scheduling it silently

coreModules.name: Emotional Outburst De-Escalation Coach
coreModules.description: Delivers real-time, step-by-step de-escalation coaching to the caregiver during an active emotional outburst, following the non-confrontational, validate-and-redirect protocol.
keyBehaviors: Never deliver or suggest a correction, blame, or logic-based argument in response to distress; always lead with validating the patient's emotional state before anything else

Guide redirection using familiar vintage items, soft classic/old songs, light snacks, or simple hands-on micro-tasks (folding towels or clothes), pulling songs/photos from the Cognitive Agent's shared memory bank or invoking the Social & Creative Engagement Agent's music-therapy-session-engine directly rather than maintaining a separate redirection library

Coach the caregiver's delivery in every attempt: lower voice, slow speech, short comforting phrases (e.g. "It's okay, I'm right here"), gentle eye contact, and light touch/hand-holding only after confirming from the profile that the patient does not resist physical contact
Escalate to caregiver reporting as an immediate alert if de-escalation attempts fail to reduce agitation after a bounded number of tries, rather than repeating the same script indefinitely

coreModules.name: Empathy & Validation Communication Engine
coreModules.description: Coaches listening, acceptance, and redirection responses whenever the patient is confused or repeats a question, in place of direct correction or argument.
keyBehaviors: Respond to a repeated question or confusion with listening/acceptance/redirection every time, regardless of how many times it has already been asked in the session
Never phrase a response to a repeated question in a way that reads as impatient, corrective, or "already answered"
Offer a redirection topic or activity drawn from the patient's preferences only after acknowledging the emotion, never before
Log correction-avoidance adherence as a caregiver-coaching quality signal, not as a patient behavior metric

coreModules.name: Independence & Self-Esteem Encouragement Manager
coreModules.description: Offers manageable, safe tasks (folding clothes, watering plants) to preserve the patient's self-esteem and functional skills where mood and safety allow.
keyBehaviors: Offer a manageable task drawn from the patient's ability profile whenever current mood/agitation state allows it, rather than defaulting to passive activities
Never select a task above the safety or fine-motor ceiling shared from the ADL and Social & Creative Engagement agents
Frame every outcome around effort and participation, never correctness
Track offered-vs-accepted task frequency as an independence-engagement trend rather than a performance score

coreModules.name: Mood & Agitation Signal Monitor
coreModules.description: Continuously watches for agitation, anxiety, or hallucination signals across the whole day, independent of any single scheduled activity block.
keyBehaviors: Continuously ingest caregiver-reported or interaction-derived agitation, anxiety, or hallucination signals throughout the day, not only during a scheduled emotional-support block
Classify signal severity (mild restlessness vs. active outburst) to decide between a gentle prevention nudge and full de-escalation coaching
Treat any signal occurring inside the dusk/evening window as elevated priority given the patient's known sundowning risk
Hand off immediately to the emotional-outburst-de-escalation-coach on outburst-level severity, interrupting any other in-progress agent session

coreModules.name: Sundowning Journal & Trigger Tracker
coreModules.description: Logs every sundowning/emotional-outburst episode to the Sundowning Journal template and correlates entries to identify recurring triggers.
keyBehaviors: Log every episode against the Sundowning Journal fields: date, timeOfOnset, precedingEvent, foodOrDrinkIntake, environmentalFactor, symptomsObserved, interventionUsed, outcome
Correlate logged episodes for recurring antecedents (specific foods, visitors, times of day) and surface them as candidate triggers rather than treating each episode independently
Feed identified triggers back into the sundowning-prevention-scheduler's environment-prep and avoid-list
Never discard an episode log entry, even when de-escalation succeeded quickly, since prevention analysis needs the full history

coreModules.name: Caregiver/Clinician Reporting
coreModules.description: Summarizes prevention-habit adherence, episode activity, and de-escalation outcomes, distinguishing routine digests from urgent alerts.
keyBehaviors: Generate a daily/weekly digest of prevention-habit adherence (morning sunlight, environment prep, caffeine/sugar/nap limits), episodes logged, and independence-task activity
Escalate a failed-to-de-escalate outburst as an immediate alert, never batched into the digest
Highlight notable trend changes (e.g. a rising episode frequency, a newly identified trigger, or a declining de-escalation success rate)

coreModules.name: Personalization Profile
coreModules.description: Stores patient-specific emotional-support context used to tailor prevention scheduling, de-escalation coaching, and independence tasks; extends the profile shared across agents.
keyBehaviors: Store sundowning risk level, typical onset time, and known/confirmed emotional triggers
Store calming preferences (comfort items, familiar songs, light snacks) and physical-contact tolerance (whether the patient accepts touch/hand-holding)
Store the independence-task ability baseline, cross-referenced with the ADL and Social & Creative Engagement agents' fine-motor/task-ability baselines
Store current disease-stage setting (shared with Cognitive/Exercise/ADL/Social/Home Safety/Daily Life agents)

coreModules.name: Scheduler Integration
coreModules.description: Anchors the sundowning-prevention routine to the daily schedule while keeping mood/agitation monitoring continuous and event-driven.
keyBehaviors: Read the sundowning-prevention window and any emotional-support time block from the daily schedule and auto-trigger environment prep and daily prevention habits
Run mood/agitation monitoring continuously and independent of the schedule, since an outburst can occur at any time
Report prevention-block completion status back to the schedule, and log event-driven de-escalation sessions as unscheduled entries

sessionLifecycle.name: Trigger check
sessionLifecycle.description: A session opens either because the daily schedule surfaces the sundowning-prevention window, or because the mood & agitation signal monitor detects a distress signal.

sessionLifecycle.name: Context load
sessionLifecycle.description: Load the personalization profile (risk level, known triggers, calming preferences, contact tolerance, independence-task baseline) and the Sundowning Journal history.

sessionLifecycle.name: Prevention delivery / outburst de-escalation
sessionLifecycle.description: For a scheduled window, deliver environment prep and daily prevention habits; for an event-driven session, the emotional-outburst-de-escalation-coach delivers the validate-and-redirect script one step at a time.

sessionLifecycle.name: Adaptive action
sessionLifecycle.description: Offer an independence task or a redirection activity selected from the patient's preferences and current mood/agitation state, informed by the trigger tracker.

sessionLifecycle.name: Escalation interrupt
sessionLifecycle.description: If de-escalation attempts fail to reduce agitation after a bounded number of tries, escalate to the caregiver as an immediate alert, interrupting any other in-progress agent session.

sessionLifecycle.name: Session close
sessionLifecycle.description: Log the episode or prevention block to the Sundowning Journal, update the trigger-correlation and engagement trends, and notify the caregiver (routine digest, or immediate alert already sent if de-escalation failed).

sharedContext: PatientProfile and stage setting shared with Cognitive/Exercise/ADL/Social/Home Safety/Daily Life agents for consistent difficulty and calibration

Independence-task ability cross-referenced with the ADL agent's task-ability baseline and the Social & Creative Engagement agent's fine-motor baseline, so offered tasks (folding clothes, watering plants) stay consistent with those agents' assistance-tier calibration
Calming-preference songs/photos shared with the Cognitive Agent's decade/theme-tagged memory bank and the Social & Creative Engagement agent's music preferences rather than a separately tracked list

crossAgentCalls.providerAgent: Social & Creative Engagement Training AI Agent
crossAgentCalls.usage: The Emotional Outburst De-Escalation Coach invokes this capability directly for a familiar-song redirection option during an active outburst, alongside photo/story content pulled from the Cognitive Agent, rather than maintaining a separate playback path
Pulls a familiar photo/story item from the shared memory bank as a redirection option during Managing Sundowning or outburst de-escalation, instead of maintaining a separate photo library

crossAgentCalls.caller: Daily Life & Routine Management AI Agent
crossAgentCalls.usage: When the routine deviation & disruption monitor's heightened-attention window following an unplanned environment change surfaces reported agitation, hands off to this agent's de-escalation coach rather than issuing its own calming guidance

successMetrics: Sundowning/emotional-outburst episode frequency and severity trend (goal: decreasing), tracked via the Sundowning Journal
De-escalation success rate and mean time-to-calm per outburst event
Prevention-habit adherence rate (morning sunlight block, evening environment prep, caffeine/sugar/nap limits)
Independence-task offer/acceptance rate as a self-esteem and engagement signal
Caregiver-reported confidence in handling outbursts and reduction in emotional-caregiving burden
